sentences.text:
Author: G. Shyam Prasad
Bench: G. Shyam Prasad
 1
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice G. Shyam Prasad
 Criminal Petition No. 6239 Of 2019
Order:

This Criminal Petition, under Section 482 Cr.P.C., is filed seeking to quash the proceedings in FIR No.192 of 2019 dt. 05.07.2019 on the file of Ongole-I Town Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 273, 420 IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

02. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
03.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submit that the petitioners are Accused Nos. 1 and 2 in FIR No.192 of 2019 dt. 05.07.2019, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 273, 420 IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
He further submits that the facts in the FIR and the facts in the Common Order dt. 27.08.2018 passed by this Court in Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2018 and batch, are one and the same.

This Court has taken a view that the Police have no jurisdiction to register the offences referred above in respect of transportation of tobacco products like Khainy Packets and Pan Masala etc., and that the transportation and selling of Tobacco products are not the offences come under the purview of the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

He further submits that in the light of the Common Order passed by this Court in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch, the respondents have no jurisdiction to register the offences punishable under Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and therefore, the petitioners are entitled for quashment of the proceedings in FIR No.192 of 2019.

04 . Learned Public Prosecutor for the State submits that the issue involved in the present Criminal Petition is squarely covered by the Common Order dt.27.08.2019 in Crl.P.N6.3731 of 2018 and batch.
05.

The contents of the complaint in the instant case reveals that the Police have caught hold of the accused Nos. 1 and 2 and seized Khaleja Gutka-81 packets, Blue Bull-35 packets, M. Tobacco Khainee-60 Packets, (4) Chaini Khaini- 17 packets, Raja Khaini-17 packets, V1 Tobacco Khainee-13 Kunchala Bhaskar Reddy, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 23 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65200071/
1 packets and M1 Raz Tobacco Khaini-2 packets from the accused, which were harmful to the human consumption.

06. The purport of the complaint is that selling of prohibited tobacco products like Khainy, Gutka etc., to the public at abnormal rates, suppressing the truth that chewing of Khaniny and Gutka etc.,
injurious to health, is liable for punishment for the offences under Sections punishable under Sections 188, 273, 420 IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
07.
In the light of the judgment referred above, there is no hesitation to come to a conclusion that similar set of petitions were allowed while quashing the proceedings.

Therefore, the Petitioners are also on the same footing to that of the petitioners in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch.
08.
Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings in FIR No.192 of 2019 on the file of Ongole-I Town Police Station, Prakasam District, are hereby quashed against the Petitioners.
